nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $S$ be a measurable space, and let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \ldots : \Omega \to S$ be measurable maps that are independent under $\mu$ and each have the same distribution under $\mu$ as $X_0$. If an event $E \subseteq \Omega$ is exchangeable with respect to $(X_n)$, then $\mu(E) = 0$ or $\mu(E) = 1$.
nodes.title: Hewitt–Savage zero–one law for i.i.d. sequences

nodes.title: Hewitt–Savage zero–one law on a Polish space

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ and $S$ be measurable spaces and let $X_0, X_1, \ldots : \Omega \to S$ be a sequence of maps. An event $E \subseteq \Omega$ is exchangeable with respect to $(X_n)$ if there is an exchangeable event $A \subseteq S^{\mathbb{N}}$ such that $E = \{\omega \in \Omega : (X_n(\omega))_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \in A\}$.
nodes.title: Event exchangeable with respect to a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a measurable space. A set $A \subseteq S^{\mathbb{N}}$ is an exchangeable (or permutable) event if it is measurable for the product σ-algebra and $\{x : x \circ \sigma \in A\} = A$ for every permutation $\sigma$ of $\mathbb{N}$ that moves only finitely many indices.
nodes.title: Exchangeable event

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ and $S$ be measurable spaces and let $X_0, X_1, \ldots : \Omega \to S$ be measurable maps. If $E \subseteq \Omega$ is exchangeable with respect to $(X_n)$, then $E$ is measurable.
nodes.title: Exchangeable events of a measurable sequence are measurable

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
